processed_clauses.metadata_title: Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর সংশোধন
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
------ অধ্যায়
Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর সংশোধন

Customs Act 1969: The document outlines amendments made to the Customs Act 1969, which serves as the foundational legislation for customs and trade operations in Bangladesh.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Act No. IV of 1969 এর section 119B এর সন্নিবেশ
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
--। Act No. IV of 1969 এর section 119B এর সন্নিবেশ।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969), অতঃপর উক্ত Act বলিয়া উল্লিখিত, এর section 119A এর পর নিম্নরূপ নূতন section 119B সন্নিবেশিত হইবে, যথা:-
“119B. Performing the operation of bonded warehouse electronically.- Notwithstanding anything contained in any other provisions of this Act or in any other law for the time being in force, the Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, declare that the operation of any bonded warehouse may be performed electronically subject to such conditions, restrictions and procedures as specified in that notification.”।

Customs Act 1969: The Act is amended to insert a new section that specifically addresses the electronic performance of bonded warehouse operations.
The provisions of this new section take precedence over any other existing laws or provisions within the Act regarding the operation of bonded warehouses.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: The operation of bonded warehouses is authorized to be conducted electronically.
The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue a notification in the official Gazette specifying the conditions, restrictions, and procedures for transitioning to electronic operations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to declare through an official Gazette notification that bonded warehouse operations may be performed electronically.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Act No. IV of 1969 এর section 156 এর সংশোধন
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
--। Act No. IV of 1969 এর section 156 এর সংশোধন।- উক্ত Act এর section 156 এর sub-section (1) এর Table এর column 1 এ বর্ণিত-
(ক) ক্রমিক নম্বর 10, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 32, 33, 34, 40, 43, 43A, 44, 45, 49, 54, 56, 59, 61, 63, 64, 65, 71 ও 75 এ বর্ণিত Offences এর বিপরীতে column 2 এ বর্ণিত Penalties এ উল্লিখিত “fifty thousand Taka” শব্দগুলির পরিবর্তে “two lakh Taka” শব্দগুলি প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে;
(খ) ক্রমিক 47A এর পরিবর্তে নিম্নবর্ণিত ক্রমিক 47A প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে, যথা:-

| “47A. If any person- (i) without lawful authority gains access to, or attempts to gain access to, any Customs computerised entry processing system; or | such person shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding twice the amount of duty taxes involved or five lakh Taka whichever is higher; and on conviction before a Magistrate, shall be further liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or to a fine not exceeding five lakh Taka, or to both. | 79B |
| (ii) without lawful authority gains access to, or attempts to gain access to, any Customs computerised entry processing system or any trade or passenger information received for the purpose of Customs clearance, uses or discloses information obtained from such system or arrangement for a purpose that is not authorized; or | such person shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding five lakh Taka; and on conviction before a Magistrate, shall be further liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or to a fine not exceeding five lakh Taka, or to both. | 79B & 204B |
| (iii) having lawful access to any Customs computerised entry processing system or any trade or passenger information received for the purpose of Customs clearance, uses or discloses information obtained from such system or arrangement for a purpose that is not authorized; or | such person shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding two lakh Taka; and on conviction before a Magistrate, shall be further liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or to fine not exceeding five lakh Taka, or to both. | 79B & 204B |
| (iv) who is not authorised to do so, receives information obtained from any Customs computerised entry processing system or from any other means for the purpose of Customs clearance, and uses, discloses, publishes or authorizes dissemination of such information, | such person shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding two lakh Taka; and on conviction before a Magistrate, shall be further liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or to fine not exceeding five lakh Taka, or to both. | 79B & 204B” । |

Customs Act 1969: The Act is amended to increase the prescribed monetary penalties associated with a range of customs offences listed in the Table of Section 156.

The amendment revises the penalties for unauthorized access, data misuse, or unauthorized disclosure involving the customs computerized system to include both administrative fines and potential criminal conviction.
Customs Offence Penalties: Specified penalties for numerous existing customs offences have been increased from fifty thousand Taka to two lakh Taka.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: Unauthorized access to or attempts to access this system now carry a penalty of up to twice the duty or a fixed maximum amount, whichever is higher, alongside potential imprisonment and further fines upon conviction.

The misuse or unauthorized disclosure of trade or passenger information obtained from the system or other customs channels is now subject to specific tiered administrative penalties and criminal liability.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Act No. IV of 1969 এর section 204B এর সন্নিবেশ
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
--। Act No. IV of 1969 এর section 204B এর সন্নিবেশ।- উক্ত Act এর section 204A এর পর নিম্নরূপ নূতন section 204B সন্নিবেশিত হইবে, যথা:-
“204B. Confidentiality and arrangement for exchange of information facilitating trade.- (1) All trade and passenger information gathered by Customs for clearance purpose shall be confidential and shall not be used except for –
(a) statistical purposes by the Board and other Government organizations; or
(b) purposes of comparison and evidence by the appropriate officer of Customs as against other imports and exports; or
(c) production as evidence before a legal proceeding or an organization explicitly so authorized by the Government; or
(d) disclosure of information subject to the condition and limitation under the Right to Information Act, 2009 (Act No. XX of 2009); or
(e) any other purposes to be determined by the Board.
(2) The Government may enter into any bilateral, regional, multilateral agreement or convention or any other arrangement to exchange of information for trade facilitation, effective risk analysis, verification of compliance and prevention, combating and investigation of offences under the provisions of this Act.
(3) The information exchanged under sub-section (2), subject to the limitation and condition provided under the agreement or convention or any such arrangement, may be used as evidence in investigations and proceedings under this Act or corresponding law of another country by which such arrangement exists.
(4) The Board shall, by notification in the official gazette, specify the procedure and conditions subject to which such exchange shall be made and designation of the person through whom such information shall be exchanged.
(5) Any disclosure, publishing or dissemination of information except as provided above without explicit permission shall be an offence.”।

Customs Act 1969: A new section 204B is inserted into the Act to establish provisions for the confidentiality of trade and passenger information and the framework for international information exchange to facilitate trade.
The Act mandates that the exchange of information and its use as evidence in investigations or legal proceedings must comply with established agreements or conventions.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to use gathered trade information for statistical purposes and to determine additional purposes for which such information may be utilized.
The Board is responsible for issuing notifications in the official gazette to specify the procedures, conditions, and designated officials for the exchange of trade information.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer is authorized to use gathered trade information for the purpose of comparing imports and exports or as evidence.
Right to Information Act 2009: The disclosure of customs information is subject to the conditions and limitations specified under this Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Act No. IV of 1969 এর FIRST SCHEDULE এর প্রতিস্থাপন
processed_clauses.resolved_text: --। Act No. IV of 1969 এর FIRST SCHEDULE এর প্রতিস্থাপন।- উক্ত Act এর FIRST SCHEDULE এর পরিবর্তে এই আইনের তফসিল-...... এ উল্লিখিত “FIRST SCHEDULE” (পৃথকভাবে মুদ্রিত) প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে।

Customs Act 1969: The Act is being updated by replacing its First Schedule with a new version as specified in the amending legislation.
The legislation mandates the substitution of the existing First Schedule in its entirety.
First Schedule: The First Schedule of the Customs Act 1969 is officially replaced by the new version provided within this legislative document.

First Schedule: The First Schedule of the Customs Act 1969 is being replaced in its entirety by the Finance Act 2022.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: The Bangladesh Customs Tariff is contained within the First Schedule and is formally referenced by Section 18 of the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Act 1969: This is the parent statute that governs customs operations and provides the legal authority for the First Schedule and the Bangladesh Customs Tariff.
